relevance_note: Family report of two brothers with biochemically diagnosed LCAT deficiency plus three obligate heterozygote sons: 'A 54-year-old man (proband) and his 58-year-old brother presented with corneal opacity'; no LCAT variant is described ('Gene analysis of the present family is now in progress').
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON assembled by a short script and every span checked verbatim against the Markdown. No variant rows: the paper identifies no LCAT variant (gene analysis 'now in progress'); homozygosity/heterozygosity is inferred by the authors from LCAT activity/mass and obligate-carrier status only. Labels: Table 2 has a 'Case' column of bare numbers 1-6; the text uses 'Case 1', 'Case 2', 'Case 4' and 'Case 6', so those keep the paper's label, while cases 3 and 5 are never named in the text and get 'Table 2 #3' and 'Table 2 #5'. Identification of Table 2 cases 3-5 as the three sons and case 6 as the proband's wife rests on Table 2 (males aged 24/23/18, female 49), 'The LCAT activity of the wife and three sons of Case 1 was determined (Table 2)', 'Lipoprotein fractions of a heterozygote, Case 4' and 'normal (Case 6)'; the wife (not a blood relative) is included as a tested family member described in relation to the proband. Abstract statements 'Both subjects showed a marked decrease in serum HDL-cholesterol and in the cholesteryl ester ratio' were used as a named-group statement for Cases 1 and 2. Ambiguous abstract statements ('Urinary examination showed microhematuria or proteinuria', 'no anemia was demonstrated', 'Although apo A-I and A-II were low') were not assigned to Case 2; they are assigned to Case 1 only where the Case 1 paragraph states them. 'HDL-C and apo A-I levels of the sons were low normal' was read as a normal finding (D-27) excluding low HDL-C and low apo A-I for the sons; the checklist item 'low apolipoprotein a-i or a-ii' stays not reported because apo A-II is not addressed. 'Normal renal function' was recorded as 'impaired renal function' excluded but not used to exclude the composite checklist item 'chronic kidney disease or renal failure' (Case 2 has marked proteinuria; CKD is broader). 'There was no evidence of ischemic heart disease or other atherosclerotic disorders in the present family' excludes atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease for all six family members (group statement). Vital status 'alive' for Cases 1 and 2 from 'They are now being followed at Nakatsugawa Municipal Hospital.' Table 2 lipid values (TG, FC, apo values) are reported without interpretation, so hypertriglyceridemia, free cholesterol etc. are not reported. OCR problems: Table 2 row 4 is column-shifted ('149 36' under TC, HDL-C blank), Table 1 and parts of the Introduction/Methods are garbled; no values were taken from garbled cells except age/sex. The Discussion's general list of LCAT-deficiency features ('These findings are observed only in homozygotes, not in heterozygotes') is a general statement and was not applied to individuals. Prior report: the work was presented as a 1993 abstract (ref 7). n_patients_reported=2 from 'two homozygotes'; cohort_size_as_stated null (six family members investigated, no patient total stated). No contradictions within the paper found.
